Subject: Clarify per-token discount ladder — marginal vs blended

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — NimbleHealth is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Procurement asked for a clear write-up on the per-token volume ladder so our finance team can model cost under two approaches:

1) Pure marginal ladder (discount applies only to tokens within each breakpoint)
2) Blended/effective rate (average per-token after applying tiered pricing across total usage)

Our baseline numbers for modeling: expected monthly usage = 120M tokens, committed ARR equivalent = 1.2B tokens annually (100M/month committed). We also want to understand:
- How breakpoints are defined (calendar month vs rolling 30d),
- True-up / undercommit clawback mechanics at year-end,
- Treatment of overage rates if we exceed commit in a month,
- Any incentive to prepay/annualize for a lower blended rate.

I've attached our rough volume profile (NimbleHealth_MonthlyVolumes.xlsx). Can you send a short, side-by-side worked example and suggested contract language for the proposals?

Appreciate it —
Tom

Subject: Re: Clarify per-token discount ladder — marginal vs blended

Tom / Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and the volume file. Below are two compact scenarios with the same committed volume (100M tokens / month). I kept the math simple so your FP&A team can drop numbers in. If you'd like we can export this to a one-page PDF for procurement.

Scenario assumptions (both): commit = 100M tokens/month; billing = monthly; model family = redwood-4.

A) Marginal ladder (pricing per-token by band) — example bands:
- 0–25M: $0.040/token
- 25M–75M: $0.035/token
- 75M–200M: $0.030/token

If actual usage in a month = 120M tokens, cost = (25M*$0.040) + (50M*$0.035) + (45M*$0.030) = $1,000,000 + $1,750,000 + $1,350,000 = $4,100,000 => effective rate = $0.034167/token.

B) Blended (committed tier yields single effective per-token rate for all tokens that month) — e.g., commit band determines single rate:
- Commit band 0–50M => $0.039/token
- Commit band 50M–150M => $0.033/token
- Commit band 150M+ => $0.029/token

With committed 100M/month, blended rate = $0.033/token => monthly cost on actual 120M = 120M*$0.033 = $3,960,000 => effective rate = $0.033/token.

Key differences (short):
- Marginal typically benefits spikey months (only top increment charged at lower band); blended benefits when committed band price is negotiated down (predictable whole-month cost).
- From vendor perspective, blended locks in a per-token expectation for forecasting and simpler billing; marginal is more market-friendly when usage pattern is variable.

Contract mechanics we recommend (draft language summary):
- Breakpoints measured per billing month (calendar month), with 30-day smoothing option as an add-on.
- Monthly overages billed at next-tier marginal rate (or at a defined overage rate = 10% premium over top band) — your preference.
- Annual true-up: reconcile committed tokens vs actual tokens over contract year; shortfall >10% triggers a 50% clawback on discounts applied (applied as an invoice).
- Prepay/annualization: 5–8% additional off blended rate for full annual prepaid credits (non-refundable, applied monthly).

Attached: redwood_commit_summary_v2.xlsx (contains sample math and two column-by-column scenarios).

Next steps: if you prefer, pick which structure (marginal vs blended) and whether you want 30d rolling smoothing + prepay incentive. We can then send a redlineable SOW and DocuSign.

Tom / Elena — quick technical notes to consider when choosing structure: 

- Token mix matters: prompt vs completion tokens and multimodal payloads shift effective cost. If Nimble's workload has a high prompt:completion ratio, per-request batching can materially reduce billable tokens; we can model both profiles.
- Model variants: quantized variants (rq4/q4f16) change per-token execution cost — we can map price tiers to model family if you expect to use cheaper quantized variants for lower-cost prediction workloads.
- Batching & caching: suggest enabling prefix KV caching for common system prompts and using continuous batching for low-latency pools — this reduces monthly billable tokens that hit the top bands.
- Reporting: we'll supply token-level telemetry (prompt/completion split) and a monthly usage export so finance can validate blended vs marginal reconciliations.

If you send a representative week of request logs (anonymized), I can run a quick simulation and show your expected effective rate under both pricing structures.

—Grace
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: internal: NimbleHealth concession ask & approval path

Aditya / Rishi —

Summary: Nimble asks for the blended option at $0.033/token on 100M commit (they modeled that as their preferred commercial outcome). They also want the annual true-up to have a softer clawback (<=25% clawback if shortfall <15%).

Recommended concession plan:
- Offer blended @ $0.033 if they (a) sign 12-month committed ARR and (b) prepay 50% of annual committed tokens (gives us cash and lowers risk).
- True-up: if annual usage < committed by >10% then clawback = 50% of discount previously applied; if shortfall 0–10% then no clawback. (This is our standard guardrail.)
- Approve one-time onboarding credit of $20k (to cover integration and pilot costs).

Please confirm if leadership should approve the blended concession (50% prepay + $20k credit) or if we push for marginal ladder only. This will be presented to Nimble next call (Thursday).

Subject: Final terms and DocuSign for NimbleHealth (blended option)

Tom / Elena —

Thanks for the productive conversation this week. Per internal approvals we can offer the blended structure with the following commercial terms: 

- Committed volume: 100M tokens/month (1.2B tokens annual)
- Blended rate: $0.033/token applied to all consumption in a billing month
- Prepay: 50% of annual committed tokens to be prepaid within 30 days of agreement execution (applied as account credit over first 6 months)
- True-up: annual reconciliation; shortfall tolerance up to 10% => no clawback; shortfall >10% => clawback = 50% of discount applied to the shortfall volume
- Overages: billed monthly at blended rate + 10% premium (unless we move them into a higher commit band)
- Onboarding credit: $20,000 one-time credit applied to first invoice

I've uploaded the SOW and a redlineable order form to DocuSign — please review and sign if this matches your expectations: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-nimble-ds

If you'd like the marginal ladder instead, we can provide that structure (same breakpoints as our example) but pricing will be marginal and we would not offer the 50% prepay discount.

Look forward to getting this across the line —
